headline: Last session: Sensex fell 289 points on inflation concerns, though markets held weekly gains

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Tuesday, 17 November.

why: Inflation concerns weighed on market sentiment during the last trading session.
Foreign institutional investor (FII) buying provided support, helping benchmark indices gain for the third straight week.
Lower crude oil prices and global fund inflows fueled earlier weekly gains across broader markets.
A retreat in AI stocks globally driven a rotation back into Indian equities.
whatHappening: Sensex dropped 289 points and Nifty slipped in the last session as inflation worries hit trading sentiment.
Smallcap stocks jumped 3.6% and PSU banks surged 7.5% over the week.
India and Egypt are preparing terms of reference for a potential trade agreement.
The RBI announced it may review the ₹3 lakh income threshold for microfinance borrowers if needed.
summary: On the last trading session, Indian markets fell as inflation concerns pressed Sensex down by 289 points. Despite the drop, benchmark indices secured gains for the third consecutive week supported by steady FII inflows and strong rallies in PSU banks and smallcaps. Looking ahead, traders are watching upcoming WPI inflation figures, crude oil price shifts, and foreign fund activity for direction.
